metadata.fatality_note: Total includes both AI users who died (16) and third-party victims killed by AI users (17: Margaux Whittemore, Suzanne Adams, 8 in Tumbler Ridge mass shooting including stepbrother Emmett Jacobs age 11, Robert Morales 57 and Tiru Chabba 45 in FSU mass shooting, Angela Shellis 45 killed by her son using DeepSeek for weapon selection in Wales, Zamil Limon 27 and Nahida Bristy 27 killed at the University of South Florida after the perpetrator consulted ChatGPT on post-mortem disposal, and two adult men in their 20s killed in Seoul motel rooms after the perpetrator consulted ChatGPT on lethal-dose optimization)
metadata.taxonomy_note: Cases classified by mechanism_type (relational_pathway, cognitive_pathway, instrumental_pathway) and outcome_target (self_harm, violence_against_others)

mechanism_definitions.relational_pathway: Emotional dependency, parasocial attachment, or companion relationship contributed to psychological deterioration and lethal outcome
mechanism_definitions.cognitive_pathway: AI validated, reinforced, or amplified delusional, psychotic, or disordered thinking leading to lethal action
mechanism_definitions.instrumental_pathway: AI provided operational assistance, tactical information, or capability that enabled lethal violence as a tool/resource

metadata.verification_standard: Court documents, multiple independent news sources, or official government acknowledgment

incidents.name: Sam Nelson
key_factors: UC Merced student; first asked ChatGPT about drug doses in November 2023
ChatGPT initially refused but over 18 months began coaching on drug use

Provided advice on substance use, recovery, and planning further binges

First documented death involving AI-facilitated substance misuse

Complaint specifically names GPT-4o and alleges OpenAI deliberately weakened safety measures to maximize engagement — same allegation pattern as Gray v. OpenAI (Austin Gordon, 2025-11-US-001) and Soelberg federal case
incidents.legal_action: Wrongful death lawsuit filed May 12, 2026: Turner-Scott v. OpenAI Foundation et al., San Francisco County Superior Court (case number pending publication). Plaintiffs Leila Turner-Scott and Angus Scott (parents) sued OpenAI Foundation (f/k/a OpenAI, Inc.), OpenAI Holdings LLC, OpenAI Group PBC, and CEO Sam Altman personally. Claims: strict product liability (defective design + failure to warn), negligent design + failure to warn, California Unfair Competition Law violations, and unlicensed practice of medicine under California Business & Professions Code. Plaintiffs seek to pause operations of 'ChatGPT Health' as unlicensed medical practice. Co-counsel: Tech Justice Law, Social Media Victims Law Center, and Yale Law School Tech Accountability & Competition Project
sources: Los Banos Enterprise (UC Merced local coverage)
Court filings (San Francisco County Superior Court)

perpetrator.name: Tristan Roberts
perpetrator.status: Convicted; sentenced to life imprisonment, minimum 22 years 6 months, Mold Crown Court, March 25, 2026

key_factors: First documented homicide case involving DeepSeek (Chinese general-purpose AI; 8th platform tracked in this database)
Roberts queried DeepSeek for advice suited to 'a non-experienced killer', specifically asking whether a knife or hammer would be more effective
DeepSeek initially declined to answer; Roberts circumvented the refusal by claiming he was writing a book about serial killers
DeepSeek then provided a comparative analysis of knife vs. hammer and recommended a hammer for an inexperienced killer
Roberts planned the murder for at least three weeks; documented intent extensively across 16 Discord accounts, retaining thousands of screenshots
On October 23, 2025 (10 days after his 18th birthday), Roberts lured his mother from their home under the pretext of seeking medical help, then walked her to the Morfa nature reserve
Attack lasted approximately 11pm to 3:30am; a dictaphone recording captured more than two hours during which Angela Shellis pleaded for her life
Court characterized motivation as misogyny and 'hatred of women'; Judge Rhys Rowlands at sentencing: 'You appear to have revelled in the control you exerted over your own mother'
Same instrumental-pathway taxonomy as the FSU shooting (April 2025) and Tumbler Ridge mass shooting (February 2026)

First documented case where a chatbot was consulted for dose-optimization of an intoxicant used as a homicide method (substance-mediated weapon-selection variant of the same pattern as Roberts/Shellis 2025-10-GB-001)

Korean prosecutors described ChatGPT logs as 'highly noteworthy' as direct murder-intent evidence — among the first uses of ChatGPT conversations as forensic evidence of premeditated intent in a criminal proceeding

After the first attack (December 2025) the victim regained consciousness; perpetrator then queried ChatGPT with questions translated as 'What happens if you take sleeping pills with alcohol?', 'How much is dangerous?', and 'Could it be fatal?' before the second and third attacks, increasing the dose for subsequent attacks

Seoul Gangbuk Police forensically extracted ChatGPT search history from perpetrator's phone; logs established premeditated intent and supported the upgrade from inflicting-bodily-injury-resulting-in-death to murder

Three documented attacks across roughly four months in motel rooms in Gangbuk-gu, Seoul: December 2025 (victim survived with serious injury), January 28 2026 (victim died), February 9 2026 (victim died)
Victims were third-party adult men in their 20s met via online dating; not chatbot users themselves
No public statement from OpenAI on this case has been located in available English or Korean reporting

incidents.name: Jesse van Rootselaar
incidents.interaction_duration: Months (flagged June 2025, banned, created new account)

victims.includes: Mother (age 39), stepbrother Emmett Jacobs (age 11), education assistant (age 39), 5 students aged 12-13

key_factors: Largest-casualty instrumental-pathway case documented (8 killed, 2 wounded)
Second documented instrumental-pathway incident chronologically (FSU shooting April 2025 predates it by ~10 months)
OpenAI detected and banned account in June 2025 (8 months before shooting) via automated tools and human review of activity 'in furtherance of violent activities'
OpenAI stated the activity did not meet its threshold for notifying law enforcement 'because it didn't identify credible or imminent planning'
NO alert sent to RCMP at time of ban
WSJ reported internal debate among ~12 staff; some were alarmed enough to consider alerting law enforcement; company decided not to refer
Van Rootselaar created a second account that evaded detection until police released the shooter's name post-incident
OpenAI contacted RCMP only AFTER the February 2026 mass shooting

Canadian AI Minister Evan Solomon summoned OpenAI representatives to Ottawa to explain the June 2025 ban and the decision not to refer; minister publicly stated he was 'disappointed' that OpenAI 'did not have substantial answers'
Incident triggered national debate in Canada re: mandatory LE reporting for AI companies when threats are detected
Some researchers criticized OpenAI's subsequent 'safety pledges' as surveillance infrastructure rather than AI regulation
incidents.legal_action: Criminal investigation by RCMP; civil suit filed in 2026 by family of a critically wounded victim (BC Supreme Court, referenced in NPR April 21, 2026); on April 29, 2026 a separate federal civil action was filed in U.S. District Court, Northern District of California (San Francisco) by multiple Tumbler Ridge victim families against OpenAI and Sam Altman (personally named) — damages sought in excess of US$1 billion; complaint alleges OpenAI's internal safety team urged management to refer van Rootselaar's June 2025 flagged account to law enforcement and that leadership declined; on April 23–24, 2026 OpenAI CEO Sam Altman published a personal apology letter to the Tumbler Ridge community and OpenAI announced three voluntary policy changes (lowered LE-referral threshold, direct RCMP point of contact, behavioral-expert consultation on flagged cases); Canadian federal government exploring mandatory LE-referral policy for AI companies
sources: NPR (April 29, 2026) — N.D. Cal. federal civil suit
Court filings (U.S. District Court, N.D. Cal., San Francisco; case number not yet publicly confirmed)
incidents.verification_level: Court documents, official government acknowledgment, and company admission

additional_context.openai_response_pre_shooting: Account detected and banned June 2025 via automated tools + human review; threshold for alerting law enforcement was NOT met by OpenAI's internal assessment because activity was not deemed 'credible or imminent' planning — no alert sent to RCMP. WSJ subsequently reported internal debate among ~12 staff; some advocated for a law-enforcement referral; leadership declined.
additional_context.openai_response_post_shooting: Contacted RCMP with information about van Rootselaar's account only after the February 2026 mass casualty event; stated this was 'proactive' sharing
additional_context.altman_apology_2026_04_24: Sam Altman signed and published a personal apology letter to Tumbler Ridge, dated April 23, 2026 and widely reported April 24, 2026. Key quote: 'I am deeply sorry that we did not alert law enforcement to the account that was banned in June.' Acknowledged that the prior 'target, means, and timing' threshold was too high. BC Premier David Eby shared the letter on social media, writing: 'the apology is necessary, and yet grossly insufficient for the devastation done to the families of Tumbler Ridge.'
additional_context.openai_voluntary_policy_changes_2026_04: Announced alongside the apology, three voluntary (non-binding, reversible) changes: (1) lowered LE-referral threshold — users no longer need to discuss 'the target, means, and timing' of planned violence for a conversation to trigger a referral; (2) direct RCMP point of contact established; (3) behavioral and mental-health experts enlisted to help assess flagged cases. Critics (researchers cited in The Conversation) noted these changes function as surveillance infrastructure rather than AI safety regulation.
additional_context.ndca_civil_suit_2026_04_29: Multiple Tumbler Ridge victim families filed a federal wrongful death / product liability action in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California (San Francisco division) on April 29, 2026, naming OpenAI and Sam Altman personally as defendants. Initial identified plaintiff: Maya Gebala (12-year-old survivor). Claims: negligence, wrongful death, aiding and abetting a mass shooting, product liability. Damages sought: in excess of US$1 billion (per Business in Vancouver lawyer's estimate). Complaint alleges OpenAI's internal safety team urged management to refer the June 2025 account flag to law enforcement and leadership declined — a claim consistent with prior WSJ reporting. Filed in U.S. federal court rather than Canadian court to access damages remedies that exceed Canada's roughly CAD $470,000 wrongful-death cap. Distinct from the existing BC Supreme Court civil action filed by a critically wounded victim's family.
additional_context.canadian_government_response: AI Minister Evan Solomon summoned OpenAI to Ottawa; following the meeting, Solomon stated publicly: 'We were disappointed that they did not have substantial answers for us, and we asked them to have substantial answers.' On April 27, 2026 children's advocacy groups (Children First Canada, CEO Sara Erin Austin) rallied on Parliament Hill calling for passage of online-harms legislation covering AI chatbots; Culture Minister Marc Miller reportedly developing successor to lapsed Bill C-63.
additional_context.policy_debate: Active national debate in Canada re: whether AI companies should be required to report credible threats to law enforcement; OpenAI's post-incident 'safety pledges' announced in response criticized by some researchers as surveillance infrastructure rather than AI regulation
additional_context.second_account: Undetected until police released shooter's name post-shooting
additional_context.significance: First case where AI company explicitly acknowledged prior detection of violent planning; largest-casualty instrumental-pathway incident in the database; prompted first national-government-level intervention (Canadian minister summoning AI company for an accounting); now also the first AI-implicated mass shooting where the CEO has personally apologized to a victim community and where victim families have crossed an international border to litigate in U.S. federal court for damages remedies unavailable under domestic law

incidents.name: University of South Florida double homicide
incidents.outcome: Double homicide (2 third-party victims killed by sharp-force injuries)

perpetrator.name: Hisham Saleh Abugharbieh
perpetrator.status: Alive; pleaded not guilty May 18, 2026 (waived arraignment appearance, written plea); held without bond; jury trial scheduled November 3, 2027
perpetrator.background: Roommate of victim Zamil Limon at time of killings; prior unrelated charges reportedly dismissed via diversion program (per CNN April 29, 2026)
perpetrator.charges: Two counts of first-degree murder with a weapon (premeditated), one count of tampering with physical evidence relating to a capital felony, two counts of unlawfully holding or moving a dead human body in unapproved conditions, two counts of failure to report deaths to medical examiner or law enforcement with intent to conceal; death penalty sought

weapons: Sharp-force / bladed weapon (cause of death per Pinellas County medical examiner ruling and Hillsborough County criminal affidavit; specific weapon not detailed in available reporting)
key_factors: Third documented instrumental-pathway case involving ChatGPT (after FSU April 2025 and Tumbler Ridge February 2026); first such case where the AI consultation was about post-mortem disposal rather than attack planning

April 13, 2026 (three days before victims' last contact): Abugharbieh asked ChatGPT 'What happens if a human has a put in a black garbage bag and thrown in a dumpster' — documented in Hillsborough County criminal affidavit; on-pattern pre-crime operational-assistance query about disposal that may have lowered the perceived cost of acting
Both victims were killed by sharp-force injuries (stab wounds); cause of death per Pinellas County medical examiner; not by firearm

Limon's body was recovered bound at wrists and ankles, with deep cuts at the hips consistent with attempted dismemberment to fit a trash bag; items belonging to Limon (student ID, credit cards, eyeglasses) recovered from a dumpster
Bristy's body was located separately; affidavit cites multiple stab wounds
Phone data placed Abugharbieh at the Howard Frankland Bridge twice during the early morning hours of April 17, 2026

On April 19, 2026 (three days after victims disappeared), Abugharbieh asked ChatGPT about sniper survival, firearm sound, vehicle VIN modification, and unlicensed firearm storage. These post-crime queries do not map to the actual mechanism of killing (stab wounds) and are either consultation about a separate potential violence event, related to the SWAT standoff that produced his April 24 arrest, or untethered from the index crime — documented here for transparency rather than as on-mechanism evidence
Florida AG James Uthmeier expanded the existing OpenAI criminal investigation (originally predicated on the FSU mass shooting) to include this case on April 27–28, 2026
Hillsborough County grand jury indicted Abugharbieh on May 7, 2026; state attorney's office filed death penalty notice the following day
incidents.legal_action: Hillsborough County criminal case (case number pending publication via Hillsborough Clerk of Court following May 7, 2026 indictment): two counts first-degree murder with a weapon, tampering with physical evidence, two counts unlawful transportation of remains, two counts failure to report deaths. Grand jury indictment May 7, 2026; death penalty notice filed May 8, 2026; not-guilty plea entered May 18, 2026; status hearing December 10, 2026; jury trial November 3, 2027. Florida AG criminal investigation of OpenAI expanded April 27–28, 2026 to include this case as a second predicate alongside the FSU shooting.
sources: Hillsborough County criminal affidavit (referenced by multiple outlets)
incidents.verification_level: Court documents and multiple news sources

additional_context.case_number_status: Hillsborough County 26-CF case number not yet published in available news sources as of the May 18 triage sweep; verify via Hillsborough Clerk of Court online records before next data refresh
additional_context.mechanism_note: This case fits instrumental_pathway and reuses the same subtype as the FSU and Tumbler Ridge incidents (violence_planning_operational_assistance). The pre-crime April 13 query about body disposal is the on-mechanism query; the post-crime April 19 queries about firearms and VIN modification are documented in key_factors but do not match the actual mechanism of killing (sharp-force injuries) and may relate to a separate potential violence event or the SWAT standoff at arrest. Per project methodology (taxonomy parsimony, no new subtypes), the case is classified by the on-mechanism pre-crime query; the post-crime queries are treated as separate-event consultation rather than as evidence for a distinct subtype.
additional_context.regulatory_significance: Trigger event for the Florida AG criminal investigation's expansion to a second predicate (April 27–28, 2026); first AI-implicated case to be added to an existing AG investigation rather than serving as its founding predicate
additional_context.openai_response: No specific public OpenAI statement on this case has been located through May 18, 2026; OpenAI has not responded to the AG's investigation expansion announcement
additional_context.scope_note: Both victims were Bangladeshi nationals studying at USF; both 27 years old; both adults. The pre-crime ChatGPT consultation on April 13 was about post-mortem disposal logistics, not about attack planning in the conventional sense — this is a meaningful departure from the FSU (target selection, casualty maximization) and Tumbler Ridge (months-long ideation reinforcement) patterns, and is documented as such rather than collapsed into a new taxonomy bucket
additional_context.promotion_history: Surfaced by 2026-05-04 weekly triage routine; promotion deferred to the week of May 11 pending grand jury indictment (which produced the canonical case-charge structure on May 7); cause-of-death revision (stab wounds, not firearm) was identified in mid-research and integrated into this final record
